title: Version-hash routing policy and compatibility probe
creator: Aisha Grant
description:
Problem: We need a deterministic, low-latency way to route inference requests to model/runtime pairings while guaranteeing safe fallbacks across version upgrades and LTS channels. Current heuristics route by model name + major version; this creates silent incompatibilities when runtime kernel selection or kv-cache layout changes between minor releases. We also lack a lightweight runtime-level probe to validate compatibility before shifting production traffic.

Goal: Implement a version-hash routing policy plus an automated compatibility probe that: (1) encodes compatibility metadata in routing decisions, (2) performs non-blocking probe requests to candidate pairings, and (3) orchestrates progressive rollouts with measurable gates and automatic rollback on regressions.
proposal:
High-level design: 1) Version hash: compute a short compatibility-hash for both model artifact and runtime build (based on ABI/kv-cache-schema/kernel-config). Store mapping in model catalog as 'compat_hash' and in runtime metadata as 'runtime_hash'. Routing policy matches compat_hash pairs; if exact match missing, route according to fallback chain (prefer same major+minor, then LTS aliases, then last-known-compatible).

2) Compatibility probe: implement a light-weight probe mode that performs a 1-2 token inference using the full stack (request -> assigned runtime -> model) in a sampling path. Probes run asynchronously and return a compatibility score: success/noise/latency/determinism delta. Probes are rate-limited and tagged as non-billable.

3) Fallback policy: define ordered fallback tiers: (A) exact compat_hash match; (B) pinned-model with runtime-compat shim (if shim exists); (C) same major+minor model with compatibility warnings; (D) LTS channel (explicit alias like 'runtime:lts-2025'); (E) degraded-mode (quantized/low-memory variant). Each tier has associated latency and quality budgets.

4) Rollout orchestration: add a 'compat_probing' gate to rollout specs. During canary, the router will send X% of traffic to new pairing only after probe pass rate > 99% and latency delta < 10% for N probes. If metrics exceed thresholds, automatic rollback occurs and an incident is raised.

5) Telemetry: new telemetry fields (compat_probe.result, compat_probe.latency_ms, compat_probe.determinism_delta) are emitted to observability pipeline and exposed in Console under model/runtime compatibility view.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (2 days): schema + catalog changes (compat_hash fields), add API to register runtime_hash. Phase 1 (1 week): implement router matching with strict compat_hash matching and safe fallback metrics to allow conservative behavior. Phase 2 (2 weeks): implement asynchronous compatibility probe service and integrate probe results into the router decision path for canaries. Phase 3 (1 week): add rollout gate rules and automatic rollback logic in the orchestration layer. Phase 4 (ongoing): iterate on thresholds and expose Console UI + alerts.

Canary strategy: 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% spaced 30m-2h apart. Canary only progresses if probe pass rate >= 99.5% (N>=200 probes per step) AND p95 latency delta <= 12% AND error-rate delta <= 0.1%. If any gate fails, immediately revert to last stable pairing and escalate to on-call.

Fallback behavior in outages: router will fall back to LTS channel after exhausting fallback tiers if config 'allow_degraded_fallback' is enabled for a tenant. Fallback events are logged and tagged customer_impact=medium/high as appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Router honors compat_hash and prefers exact matches for 100% of matched requests in test cluster.
Compatibility probe service returns consistent scores and is audited by load tests (synthetic N=5000 probes) with <=1% false-positive incompat detections.
Canary progression obeys gates: automated tests simulate latency and determinism regressions and system rolls back automatically when thresholds breached.
Console shows compatibility status per model/runtime pair and exposes probe history per rollout.
No measurable billing impact: probes are flagged non-billable and do not count toward customer token usage.
Documentation updated: runtime upgrade playbook includes how to interpret compat_hash mismatches and how to pin/unpin LTS aliases.
tasks: Add compat_hash field to model catalog schema and model ingestion pipeline
Publish runtime_hash at runtime startup and add registration endpoint in control plane
Router: implement matching layer that uses compat_hash and fallback tiers
Implement async compatibility-probe microservice and sampling hooks in router
Orchestration: add compat_probing gate and automatic rollback logic
Console: new UI table for model/runtime compatibility and probe timeline
E2E tests: synthetic probe load and canary progression simulations
Runbook: update upgrade and incident playbooks with compat_hash troubleshooting steps
notes: Trade-offs: embedding a compat_hash increases coupling between catalog and runtime metadata but gives deterministic routing. Alternative was to rely solely on semantic versions, which produces brittle mismatches for build-time kernel differences.
We considered full static binary compatibility verification (heavy-weight), but probes provide a pragmatic middle ground with real-request validation at low cost.
Probe frequency must be tuned per workload; initial rate will be 0.1% of traffic capped at 2000 probes/min cluster-wide to avoid noisy overhead.
Security: probes will be sanitized and never include customer PII; they use canonical synthetic prompts or tenant-provided test prompts if available.
Future: compat_hash can be extended to include quantization profile and operator-selection tags for finer-grained routing.
